description.value: American cloud computing company specializing in a SaaS incident management platform for IT operations departments.
A U.S. cloud software company that sells a SaaS incident management platform for IT operations teams.
PagerDuty sells an AI-first operations platform for managing incidents, from detection through resolution and prevention.
Describes itself as a digital operations management platform, which it has built out from a single on-call tool.

product_description.value: SRE Agent (detects, triages, diagnoses, and works to fix incidents), Scribe Agent (documents incidents and drafts postmortems), Shift Agent (on-call handoffs and shift summaries), Insights Agent (trends across incidents), incident management with smart alerting and unified response in Slack, Microsoft Teams, mobile, and web, and 750+ integrations with open APIs and MCP support.
PagerDuty Operations Cloud, which bundles AIOps, automation, customer service operations, and incident management with a generative AI assistant; over 700 integrations.

business_model_description.value: Most revenue comes from cloud-hosted software subscription fees plus term-license software subscription fees, sold land-and-expand. The FY2026 10-K says it has begun offering usage-based pricing and multiyear platform agreements instead of single-year, seat-based licenses.

customer_description.value: 70% of the Fortune 100 trust the platform; named customers include FOX, Zoom, Spotify, Twilio, TUI, Cox Automotive, SAP, Cloudflare, Ryanair, DraftKings, checkout.com, IAG Loyalty, and New York Life.
Increasingly focused on enterprise customers, though the platform serves companies of any size, from small to mid-market to enterprise.
Targets IT operations departments; the page names no specific customers.
